stages.name: Impact of protectionism on government
stages.title: Impact of protectionism on government
stages.sub: Weigh up why a government might gain and lose from putting up a tariff.

steps.q: A government puts a £50 tariff on every imported car. Cars still get imported. Does the government collect any money from this?
steps.right: Yes, money from every car brought in
steps.wrong: No, tariffs cost the government money
steps.hint: Who pays the tariff at the border, and where does that payment go?

steps.q: Another country's car industry is badly hurt by this tariff. Is their government likely to just accept the lost sales?
steps.right: No, it will likely hit back with its own tariffs
steps.wrong: Yes, it will accept the loss quietly
steps.hint: If your exports were suddenly blocked, would your government sit still?

steps.q: That other country now places tariffs on the first country's exports. What happens to those exports?
steps.hint: If your goods now cost more abroad because of a new tariff, what happens to sales there?

steps.q: The harmed trading partner could instead take the tariff to the body that settles trade disagreements. What might it do there?
steps.hint: Think about what the WTO exists to handle between arguing countries.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: So does a tariff leave a government simply better off, or gaining revenue while risking retaliation?
steps.wrong: Simply better off with no real risk
steps.hint: Weigh the money collected against lost exports and possible disputes.
